payload.title: Execute canonical ClayCode BASE14 closure on Andreas Ubuntu
payload.work_clay: On the registered Andreas Ubuntu developer system, start from a clean current-main checkout and execute exactly: python tools/claycode_run_andreas_target_acceptance.py . It must verify the owner-registered target fingerprint, execute the clean target component gate, full frozen FRANK H1/H2/H3 handoff, hardened ten-application target suite, real per-application receipts, strict target acceptance assembly, independent WP14 audit and receipt-gated workspace promoter. If any step fails, preserve all failure/negative receipts, identify the narrowest executable counterexample, repair implementation/orchestration without weakening any acceptance, authority or evidence gate, and rerun from evidence. Repeat until the command exits 0 and independent rereads prove 14/14 work packages PASS and 10/10 applications PASS. Then review the generated diff, commit implementation + target evidence + workspace promotion atomically through the repository single-writer path, push, and reread remote evidence.
payload.reason_clay: Cloud workers cannot honestly execute the physical Andreas Ubuntu target. The repository now has one fail-closed target closure command whose workspace promoter consumes only a passing independent WP14 manifest. Local execution is the remaining required truth surface.
payload.completion_clay: Complete only if tools/claycode_run_andreas_target_acceptance.py exits 0 on the registered Andreas Ubuntu host; ANDREAS_BASE14_CLOSURE_RUN.json has overall_pass=true; CLAYCODE_GENERAL_PURPOSE_COMPILER_MANIFEST.json has general_purpose_gate_pass=true, claycode_release_gate_pass=true, promotion_allowed=true and zero failed_work_packages; CLAYCODE_RELEASE_WORKSPACE.json rereads as BASE_PASS with every CC-WP-01..14 status=PASS and all ten required apps PASS; FULL_FRANK H1/H2/H3 evidence preserves the authority boundary; and the remote GitHub reread preserves those facts. Otherwise keep work OPEN with exact failure receipts.
